title: Seasons & Weather Expressions
description: Describe the four seasons and current weather conditions using adjectives and 'It is...'.
objectives: Name the four seasons (spring, summer, autumn/fall, winter)
Use dummy pronoun 'It' to describe weather (It is sunny, it is raining, it is windy)
Differentiate between weather nouns (rain, sun, wind) and adjectives (rainy, sunny, windy)

vocabularyList.definition: The season after winter and before summer, in which vegetation begins to grow.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Islamabad looks stunning in spring with blooming flowers.

vocabularyList.definition: The warmest season of the year, in the northern hemisphere from June to August.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: We drink cool lemon water during the hot summer.

vocabularyList.definition: The season after summer and before winter to which leaves turn golden; also called fall.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Leaves turn golden and drop in autumn.

vocabularyList.definition: The coldest season of the year, in the northern hemisphere from December to February.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Snow covers the mountains in winter.
It is a pleasant and sunny afternoon.

vocabularyList.definition: Having a great deal of rainfall.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Take an umbrella on rainy days.

vocabularyList.definition: Covered with or characterized by clouds.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The sky is dark and cloudy today.

vocabularyList.definition: Marked by or exposed to strong winds.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: It is too windy to play badminton outside.

vocabularyList.definition: Of or at a low or relatively low temperature.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The winter night is freezing cold.

vocabularyList.definition: Of or at a fairly or comfortably high temperature.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The spring sunshine feels comfortably warm.

sections.title: Weather Grammar & The Dummy 'It'
sections.content:
In English, we describe weather using the **dummy subject 'It'**:
- *What's the weather like?*
- *It is sunny.* / *It is cloudy.* / *It is hot.*

### Noun vs. Adjective Patterns
- **Noun (The weather feature)**: *sun, rain, cloud, wind, snow*.
- **Adjective (-y suffix)**: *sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, snowy*.
- **Verb in continuous**: *It is raining*, *It is snowing*.

callouts.title: Autumn vs. Fall
callouts.text: **Autumn** is standard British and Pakistani English. In American English, the same season is widely called **fall** because leaves fall from the trees.

callouts.title: Always Include 'It is'
callouts.text: Never say 'Today is rainy' alone; standard natural English requires the dummy pronoun: **It is rainy today**.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Four seasons: spring, summer, autumn (or fall), winter.
Use dummy pronoun 'It' for weather (It is sunny, it is raining, it is cold).
Weather adjectives end in -y: sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, snowy.
Autumn is the British English term; Fall is the American English term.
Seasons take preposition IN (in summer, in winter).
